analysis.subject: history
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers shift toward independence from spring 1775 onward, Lee Resolution introduced June 7 1776 with three parts, Congress response June 11 1776 with three committees, July adoption of declaration, vote of 12 colonies and New York July 9 1776, and later treaty and confederation timelines.

overview.headline: Lee Resolution Proposes Independence and Leads to Declaration

keyPoints.point: Richard Henry Lee introduced resolution proposing independence on June 7 1776
keyPoints.quote: On June 7, 1776, Richard Henry Lee introduced a resolution

keyPoints.point: Lee Resolution contained three parts including declaration of independence and foreign alliances
keyPoints.quote: The Lee Resolution contained three parts: a declaration of independence, a call to form foreign alliances, and "a plan for confederation."

keyPoints.point: Congress appointed three concurrent committees on June 11 1776 in response to resolution
keyPoints.quote: On June 11, 1776, the Congress appointed three concurrent committees in response to the Lee Resolution

keyPoints.point: Approval deferred until July when Congress adopted first part of declaration
keyPoints.quote: approval was deferred until July 2. On that date, Congress adopted the first part (the declaration).

keyTerms.gloss: proposal containing three parts including declaration of independence and plan for confederation
keyTerms.quote: The Lee Resolution contained three parts: a declaration of independence, a call to form foreign alliances, and "a plan for confederation."

keyTerms.gloss: gathering of delegates that became governing body during Revolution
keyTerms.quote: The colonists elected delegates to attend a Continental Congress that eventually became the governing body of the union during the Revolution.

keyTerms.gloss: effort to restore friendly relations with Britain after abandoning hope
keyTerms.quote: In less than a year, most of the delegates abandoned hope of reconciliation with Britain.

keyTerms.gloss: form of union planned for independent states to prepare cooperation
keyTerms.quote: a third to "prepare and digest the form of a confederation."

keyTerms.gloss: planned partnerships with other nations reflected in alliances proposal
keyTerms.quote: a second to draw up a plan "for forming foreign alliances,"
